note: Sanctioned VIP Design System compositions. `signature` is the normalized component tree — a node is `[name, ...children]`, matching is containment rather than equality, and anything under four nodes the engine ignores as too generic to check. Namespaced parts are written as the code writes them (`Dropdown.Item`, `Accordion.Root`); `canonical` is always the name the file imports (`Dropdown`, `Accordion`). **Anatomy entries** record a shape the library requires — a `Table` is rows of cells in every file that has one — and carry `canonical` set to the root import, so they keep `patterns/unregistered-composite` quiet about mandatory structure and never produce a finding of their own. **Judgement entries** record a composite with a right and a wrong form. `NewDialog.Root` and `Drawer` take their regions as props (`trigger`, `title`, `description`, `content`), which a signature does not see, so neither has an anatomy entry. Entries with no `canonical` are shapes the package does not ship: the first project to need one extracts it and fills `canonical` in. Seeded from composites that already recur in a real VIP Design System codebase (2026-09-24).

patterns.summary: The parts a Table is made of.
patterns.use: Every table. Recorded so rows of cells are not reported as an unregistered composite — including a row component that renders `TableRow(TableCell, …)` without importing `Table` itself.

patterns.summary: The parts a Dropdown menu is made of.
patterns.use: Commands on a thing. The trigger is `Dropdown.Root`'s `trigger` prop; the items are its children.

patterns.summary: The parts an Accordion is made of.
The parts a Tabs set is made of.
Asking the user to confirm an action before it happens.
patterns.use: Any destructive or irreversible action, and any action that needs a second look. `trigger`, `title`, `description`, `label` for the confirm button, `buttonVariant`, `onConfirm`.
instead_of: A NewDialog.Root whose content is a message and a Cancel/Confirm Button pair — NewConfirmationDialog already is that, with the button order and focus handling fixed
patterns.note: The anti-shape is prose rather than an `instead_of_signature`: `NewDialog.Root` carries its content as a prop, so the Cancel/Confirm pair never appears as its JSX child, and a form dialog also ends in two buttons.

patterns.summary: A button whose action is in flight.
patterns.use: `<Button loading>` — or `ButtonSubmit` for a form's submit — which draws the spinner beside the label, disables the button and sets `aria-busy`.
instead_of: A Spinner rendered inside a Button's children while a flag is set — `{ loading && <Spinner size={ 14 } sx={ { mr: 2 } } /> }`
patterns.note: The anti-shape is the action row it usually sits in, because `Button(Spinner)` alone is under the four-node floor. No `canonical`: every file that builds it already imports `Button`, which would read as deliberate.

patterns.summary: A setting switched on and off in place: a Label and a Toggle on one row, with help text under them.
patterns.use: Settings forms. The Label's `htmlFor` names the Toggle's `id`, and the help text's `id` is the Toggle's `aria-describedby`.
instead_of: Rebuilding the row per form, with the label/toggle/description wiring re-typed each time
patterns.note: Not shipped. `ToggleRow` is a different shape — a list row with a `Heading` title, an optional image and badge, and no `<label>` association — so it is not a drop-in for this. Projects assemble this row by hand; the first one extracted becomes `canonical`, and the rest import it.
